title: RAW UNASSESSED: f45r inherits an earlier ordered description body while retaining separate local fields
summary: A finite authored descendant of IDEA903 and IDEA1059: only the two licensed joined forms OPCHALDY and DALDY copy an earlier record's fully expanded ordered A-body; the separate KOL DY event adds KOL locally. The other four field types B are not copied. Original R1 source/grouping is preserved, but its two DY entity-identities are explicitly relinquished. This is an exploratory whole-page content-copy interpretation, not a universal DY meaning or confirmed native prediction.

design.fixed_scope: Exactly the already admitted86IT f45r groups in their three source-marked paragraphs. Retain all original group spellings, order, gaps, paragraph metadata and the existing finite R1 occurrence grouping. No source position is deleted, collapsed, moved or normalized. Alternate readers remain qualified evidence, not pooled copies or silently repaired variants.
design.authored_source_program: One finite ordered event program, supplied by the unchanged R1 trace and the explicitly changed event table. Each event retains its original source span and exact spelling. Its content operations are APPEND_A(descriptor), COPY_A(earlier_record), or an unchanged non-DY B-field contribution/reference. This finite supplied grouping is apparatus; the reader does not infer a universal parser or an unpriced role for an arbitrary unseen word.
design.A_body: For each paragraph record, A is an ordered list of untranslated whole-description occurrences. It is not a physical individual's complete property set. Begin that paragraph's A as empty. Ordinary R1 description events append their whole descriptor, preserving order and repeated occurrences.
design.joined_copy_rule: Only this page's licensed OPCHALDY and DALDY events mean COPY_A in this authored version. At the event, append an exact copy of the uniquely matched earlier completed paragraph's fully expanded A. The match uses the original written ordinary OPCHAL or DAL anchor, with the same source-paragraph choice as R1. Insert the entire copied block at that precise event position; do not overwrite preceding local items, reorder the block or remove duplicates.
design.free_DY_rule: The sole already grouped KOL DY event appends the untranslated descriptor KOL to the current A-body. Both original written groups remain in provenance. It no longer constrains a DY entity-field value. This finite separate-versus-joined distinction is an added authoring assumption, not established native morphology or a general rule for all free DY.
design.B_fields: Keep all non-DY R1 field events, their descriptors, field-value variables and actual earlier-record references. COPY_A does not clone these fields, their constraints or their references from the copied record. The other four field types remain local as specified by R1. No assertion is made that they are ingredients, indications, quantities or any other translated content.
design.anchor_discipline: Only ordinary description occurrences actually written in earlier completed paragraphs nominate source-record anchors. Inherited A-items never become new written anchors. All four original reference events keep their original paragraph choices, but the two DY references now transmit A-content instead of subject identity. No latest-compatible fallback, current-paragraph search, hidden initial record or forward repair is added.
design.finite_writer: Given this finite authored program and its explicit original source-span spelling table, print each event in original source order with the retained separators and paragraph boundaries. Ordinary and non-DY B events retain their old spellings. The two COPY_A events print their separately licensed joined forms; the local KOL append prints its two-group KOL DY spelling. This is a source-preserving realization of the finite program, not a spelling law choosing freely among equivalent programs, a shortest-copy compressor or an encoder of unrestricted prose.
design.finite_reader: Using the same paid R1 grouping and finite event licenses, recover the source event program from its retained spans and evaluate it paragraph by paragraph. APPEND_A adds its occurrence; COPY_A expands only the earlier completed A-list; B events retain their separate R1 effect. Preserve the exact program, source positions and expansion origins as well as the expanded A and B outputs. Reprinting the recovered finite program must preserve the source. Expanded A alone need not determine whether items were literal or copied, so no inverse from expanded content alone is claimed.
design.termination_and_reference: Every copied body comes from an earlier completed paragraph. Expansion is therefore finite and acyclic on this three-paragraph program. Copying preserves description occurrence order and multiplicity but does not create physical substances, individuals or repeated actions merely by duplicating descriptors.
design.prospective_content_consequence_from_pla: The plan states that P2 receives the complete27-item ordinary A-body of P1. P3 subsequently receives expanded P2, alongside its own local descriptions and the explicit KOL append. Earlier CHOL/YKEOL doublets survive through two levels of expansion. P1 CTHY/DAIIN field content is not included merely because A is copied. These are planned obligations to be checked by root's author/validator, not independently computed results of this producer.
design.difference_from_R1: An earlier record's description content now affects the later expanded A even without asserting that the two described subjects are identical. Conversely the old two DY entity-identities are not preserved in parallel. The free KOL DY event also changes type. This is an explicit descendant, not a claim that all R1 semantics remain true under a new label.
design.small_source_only_illustration: If earlier A=[u,v,v] and B_s=[z], and a later program writes APPEND_A(w), COPY_A(earlier), APPEND_A(r), its expanded A is [w,u,v,v,r]. It does not inherit B_s=[z]. Altering the earlier u changes the later copied content; deleting one v changes its multiplicity. The letters here are anonymous source descriptors, not Voynich glosses or additional native assignments.
binder_debt_and_known_counters: R1's paragraph, ordinary-description and field roles remain authored assumptions. Exact source accounting cannot identify those roles or meanings.
The original prior-record choices are retained as hypotheses. A matching descriptive word does not independently prove a record name or a unique physical referent.

Only two joined forms and one free DY event have new finite licenses. Existing DY distributions, joined/split alternatives and label cases do not support exporting COPY_A to all XDY or DY. Unlicensed forms remain outside this finite rule.
The old DY entity constraints cannot also be claimed after replacing them by A-copy operations. Remaining B references are preserved separately.

A whole-record-copy rival with explicitly paid replacement of B may produce the same observable content. Field differences alone do not universally refute that rival; a literal fresh-description account also remains.

The copied A contains qoky/qokaiin alongside later oky/okaiin according to the plan. Combining this body interpretation with the separate signed-R1 complement rule and a fixed same-state bearer produces a clash. Neither q-negation nor time changes are adopted to repair it.

Order and duplicates are retained as content-list occurrences. This does not yet establish what their repetition contributes in an actual historical language or how a later physical operation consumes them.
No complete historical writer, native glyph key, statistical spelling law or translated clause is supplied. Consistency of this finite authored program is not semantic confirmation.

prior_and_profile_pointers.interpretation: 903's existing source comparison motivates selective inheritance but is not a discovery of native copying and supplies no word key. R1's earlier failures/limitations remain. The profile receipt is root-owned and was not opened for new data by this producer. Root's689field-end sister dispatch is not treated as prior-record body inheritance.

design.novelty_scope: The retained difference is this explicitly paid finite body-copy descendant with unchanged source grouping and dropped DY entity identities. It is not novelty of copying, a new meaning of an entire suffix family, or a new general reference theory. Bounded duplicates returned R1/Q1/Q2 and local DAL shape evidence, not this exact operation table.
design.claim_ceiling: RAW_UNASSESSED exploratory authoring on existing exposed text. No native prediction, semantic winner, confirmed word, universal DY, physical entity identity, new data result or statistical fit. Root's separate accounting outcomes are not read or reported here.

relations.detail: Explicit new finite descendant; original selective-field proposal unchanged.
Keeps original source/grouping and anchor choices, explicitly replaces DY entity identities by body-copy content.
